---
title: "Functions"
format: html
---

Reusable helpers. Each takes its inputs as arguments and reads no global objects, and each is tested on synthetic data with a known answer in [`tests/test-functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/tests/test-functions.R).

Each section names the function under its heading, explains what it does, and then links to where it is used: the steps of the analysis that call it, and any function on this page that calls it.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/functions.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/setup.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/functions.R")
```

## Yes/no fields

`any_yes()`

The CMS-2728 form records comorbidities and insurance as yes, no or unknown. A condition counts as present only when a field is "YES"; missing or unknown counts as not present. The original code returned missing for missing fields, which would drop patients from the models; the published sample sizes show the paper's models did not.

**Used in the analysis:** 3. USRDS patient data: [Patient variables](prepare_patients.qmd#patient-variables).

**Called by:** [`derive_insurance()`](#insurance).

```{r}
#| label: fn-any-yes
#| eval: false
```

## Nephrology care

`derive_nephrology_care()`

Whether the patient saw a nephrologist before kidney failure: none, some or unknown, as in the paper's Table 1 and Model 3. Unknown is its own level, so the models keep the patients the paper kept.

**Used in the analysis:** 3. USRDS patient data: [Patient variables](prepare_patients.qmd#patient-variables).

## Dartmouth codes

`clean_dartmouth_codes()`

Sets Dartmouth's -88888 and -99999 to missing. The original code turned every negative value positive, which would have entered suppressed HSAs as 88,888 or 99,999.

**Used in the analysis:** 1. Public area data: [HSA benchmarks](download_public_data.qmd#hsa-benchmarks).


## Unique keys

`assert_unique()`

Stops if any key appears more than once, and otherwise passes the data on, so it can end a pipeline. Every lookup table is checked this way before it is joined to patients.

**Used in the analysis:**

-   1\. Public area data: [ZIP code to HSA](download_public_data.qmd#zip-code-to-hsa), [ZIP code to ZCTA](download_public_data.qmd#zip-code-to-zcta), [American Community Survey](download_public_data.qmd#american-community-survey), [Rural-urban type](download_public_data.qmd#rural-urban-type)
-   4\. Linking area data: [Cause of kidney failure mapping](link_area_data.qmd#cause-of-kidney-failure-mapping)
-   5\. Cohort flowchart: [The cohort](create_cohort.qmd#the-cohort)

```{r}
#| label: fn-assert-unique
#| eval: false
```

## Category labels

`density_category_labels()`

The labels of the five categories, built from the three cut points rounded to two decimals: 0, then >0 to the first cut point, the two middle ranges, and above the third cut point.

**Called by:** [`categorize_density()`](#density-categories).

```{r}
#| label: fn-density-category-labels
#| eval: false
```

## Density categories

`categorize_density()`

Zero facilities is its own category; the other four are cut at the quartiles, each including its upper bound, as in the original code. It stops unless there are exactly three cut points in increasing order.

**Used in the analysis:** 6. Density categories: [Categories](define_exposure.qmd#categories).

```{r}
#| label: fn-density-categories
#| eval: false
```

## Density effects

`density_effects()`

Extracts the density terms of a fitted model with Wald confidence intervals and the number of patients the model used: odds ratios for logistic models, differences for linear ones.

**Called by:** [`density_odds_ratios()`](#odds-ratios).

```{r}
#| label: fn-density-effects
#| eval: false
```

`check_votes()`

Stops unless the model answered every code exactly once, invented no code, and used only the six category names.

## Saving each provider's answers

`cached_votes()`

Saves a provider's checked answers the first time and reads them back on a rerun, so a failure in one provider never means paying the others again.

**Used in the analysis:** 2. Cause of kidney failure: [Running, checking and saving each model](classify_esrd_causes.qmd#running-checking-and-saving-each-model).

## Combining the models

`ensemble_agreement()`

One row per code with each model's category and reason; a category is accepted when at least `min_agreement` models give it (two of three in this project).

**Used in the analysis:** 2. Cause of kidney failure: [Agreement](classify_esrd_causes.qmd#agreement).

```{r}
#| label: fn-ensemble-agreement
#| eval: false
```

## Reporting the local models

`local_model_report()`

For each model that answers but does not vote: how many codes it answered once with a code from the list, how many it left unanswered, how many answers carried text that is not a code in the list, how many codes it answered more than once, and how often it gave the category the voting models accepted. Tested on synthetic answers with a known count of each.

**Used in the analysis:** 2. Cause of kidney failure: [What the local models showed](classify_esrd_causes.qmd#what-the-local-models-showed).

```{r}
#| label: fn-local-model-report
#| eval: false
```
